subject: astronomy
title: Gravity & Orbits: Why Planets Orbit
welcome_lead: Falling sideways forever — that's basically what planets do.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: orbit speed, ellipses, Newton's cannonball.
final_note: If you fall fast enough sideways, you keep missing the ground.

concepts.def: Orbit shaped like a perfect circle.
How fast an object moves in orbit.
Scientist who explained gravity and orbits.

walkthroughs.body_html: Imagine firing a cannon faster and faster from a tall mountain. Slow shots fall to the ground. A fast enough shot keeps falling but never hits — it orbits.
Most orbits are slightly elliptical (oval). Planets move a little faster when closer to the Sun and slower when further away.
Closer orbits need higher speeds. The ISS at ~400 km altitude moves at ~28,000 km/h to stay up.
